title: Trace
description: OOCC execution trace envelope. PRD docs/PRD.md §3.1-3.3. This file is append-only: existing fields, enum members, and $defs must not be removed or repurposed after release. Add new optional fields or new enum members only, and bump schema_version's minor component in the same PR.

schema_version.description: Contract version, e.g. "1.0". Bump the minor component for additive changes.

language.description: Source language the trace was produced from. §3.5 requires C++ to reuse this same contract.

source_hash.description: sha256 of the exact source text that was executed. Used as the cache key (§4.4) and for wasm artifact caching (§3.5).

steps.description: The full step-by-step trace. May be a truncated prefix/suffix per §3.3 when meta.truncated is true.

allOf.description: status in {runtime_error, compile_error} must carry a populated error object. A truncated or failed run is still a valid, playable trace, never an exception.

step_count.description: Number of steps actually recorded in `steps` (may be less than the executed step count when truncated).

truncated.description: True when `steps` does not contain every executed step. §3.3: on step_limit breach, keep first 40k + last 10k.

ExecutionError.description: Populated when status is runtime_error or compile_error.

step.description: Index into `steps` (or the pre-truncation step count) where the error occurred.

Value.description: The {val:...}/{ref:"oN"} encoding (§3.2). Primitives inline as {val}; anything else is a heap reference. Bare JSON null is accepted as shorthand wherever a Value is expected (e.g. a None-valued object field) and is equivalent to {"val": null, "repr": "None"} — reconciles the worked TreeNode example in §3.2, where `"right": null` appears unwrapped, with the value-encoding paragraph's stated rule that null is {"val": null}.

ValueInline.description: A primitive inlined directly in the trace, e.g. {"val": 4}.

repr.description: Optional display form, e.g. "None" for a Python None val.

Frame.description: One entry in Step.stack. Index 0 of the enclosing array is the outermost frame.

locals.description: Local variable bindings for this frame at this step.

args.description: Parameter names in call order, present on frames pushed by a call.

call_site_line.description: Line in the caller's frame that made this call.

ChangedPath.description: The `changed` path grammar (§3.2): frame_id.local | oN[index] | oN.field | oN{key}.

func.description: Name of the function owning this step (top of stack).

heap.description: Full snapshot of reachable non-primitives at this step, keyed by heap id. §3.4 (Phase 6): present on keyframe steps only (every 50th step by position, plus step 0). Non-keyframe steps carry `heap_patch` instead — never both, never neither. A trace produced before Phase 6's wire optimization shipped has `heap` on every step and no `heap_patch` at all, which is still a fully valid trace (every step is trivially its own keyframe); consumers must not assume every trace uses the interval scheme.

heap_patch.description: §3.4 (Phase 6): an RFC 6902 JSON Patch, `add`/`remove`/`replace` only, from the previous step's *reconstructed* heap to this step's heap. Present on non-keyframe steps instead of `heap`. Paths are JSON Pointers into the heap object, e.g. "/o1/items/4/val". Reconstruct by walking back to the nearest preceding step with `heap` set and applying every intervening step's `heap_patch` in order — see apps/web/lib/player/getStateAt.ts, the one seam every component reads trace state through.

changed.description: Paths mutated since the previous step. Drives every highlight animation — must be exact.

heap_truncated.description: True when this step exceeded the 5,000 heap-objects-per-step cap (§3.3) and deep-snapshotting was stopped.

allOf.description: `returned` is present if and only if event == "return".

JsonPatchOp.description: One RFC 6902 operation. Phase 6's diff only ever emits add/remove/replace (never move/copy/test), so those are the only ops modeled here — a hand-written JSON Patch elsewhere in the trace is not a supported input.

HeapObject.description: A heap-resident value. §3.2 lists list, tuple, dict, set, str (>40 chars), object/instance (fields), function, and the opaque fallback. An object/instance uses its class name as the `type` discriminator (see the worked TreeNode example in §3.2), so `type` is unconstrained beyond excluding the reserved primitive discriminators handled by the other branches.

entries.description: Insertion-ordered key/value pairs. A list (not a JSON object) because Python dict keys need not be strings.

HeapStr.description: Strings longer than 40 chars move to the heap; shorter strings stay inlined as {val: "..."}.

HeapOpaque.description: Fallback for any value the tracer can't project into a richer type.

HeapInstance.description: object (with fields) / instance of a user class. `type` is the class name, e.g. "TreeNode".
